reviews.text:
Serious Safety Issue Please Review Product Recommendations. As a licensed esthetician in California, I was extremely concerned when the app recommended The Ordinary AHA 30% + BHA 2% Peeling Solution for nightly use. This is a highly potent chemical exfoliant that is explicitly not safe for daily application.

Industry guidelines and the brand itself recommend using this product no more than 1 2 times per week, for no longer than 10 minutes per session. Nightly use could lead to over-exfoliation, burns, severe irritation, and long-term damage to the skin barrier.

It is critical that skincare apps provide safe, accurate product usage guidelines. Recommending this type of product for nightly use is not only inappropriate, it could genuinely harm users who trust the app’s advice.

reviews.text:
Great for learning skincare and building a routine. I’ve been using Lovi’s skincare app for a while now, and overall I really like it. I understand why some people feel disappointed or even “scammed” at first the app offers custom skincare recommendations, but the subscription fee doesn’t include the actual products. It just tells you what to buy.

That said, I personally use it a bit differently. I’ve been applying what I learn to the products I already have at home, and it’s been a really positive experience. The app has short lessons on things like lymphatic drainage massage, tricks for puffy eyes, and how to layer products properly. I’ve never really understood skincare before what goes on first, what each thing does so the structured guidance has been a big help.

Even just following a daily routine and paying attention to technique has improved my skin, without me having to buy everything they recommend right away. I’ve only started purchasing their suggested products gradually as I finish what I already own. I can see how it might feel expensive if someone tried to buy everything up front, but used gradually, it’s manageable.

The built-in AI assistant is surprisingly knowledgeable, too. It doesn’t just give canned responses it actually takes into account the products I’m using and offers tips or cautions based on ingredients and skin reactions.

In short, I think Lovi is great for learning skincare fundamentals, building good habits, and getting personalized advice. It might not be for everyone, especially if you expect the subscription to cover the products themselves, but for me it’s been genuinely educational and motivating.

The only thing I do wish was different is that I would like to be able to go back more than 3 days in the prior days because there were some really interesting lessons at the start that I would love access to again.
